perspective:
Vincent’s available information:

- He knows Patrick is his long-time friend from their teenage years; they share blue-collar work and sometimes collaborate.
- At the diner, Vincent heard Patrick say he was considering a new construction venture as an opportunity to expand his business. Patrick said it seemed worth the risk but that he was still weighing options. Vincent expressed concern about risk and financial security, suggested reconsidering or delaying until more information, and Patrick said he appreciated the concern and would think it over.
- Over the next few days, Vincent noticed Patrick avoiding detailed discussion about the investment.
- At Patrick’s construction site, Vincent told Patrick he felt Patrick was not telling him everything. Patrick said it was complicated and he didn’t want to worry Vincent with details. Vincent said he felt betrayed as a friend by the lack of transparency. Patrick apologized, said he should have been more open, and offered to sit down and explain everything.
- At Vincent’s garage, during that detailed discussion, Vincent learned the situation was serious. Patrick told him it had been tough and that he might lose a significant amount if things didn’t turn around soon. Vincent offered to lend Patrick money to cover short-term losses. Patrick thanked him and said he was grateful.
- A month later at a coffee shop, Vincent said the venture might actually turn a profit. Patrick confirmed it was starting to look up and said he was relieved they stuck with it. Vincent apologized for doubting him earlier and proposed a joint venture. Patrick agreed and said they should work out the details.
- At Vincent’s house, Vincent and Patrick were optimistic about the joint venture. Vincent said their combined skills could make it a success. Patrick agreed he was excited. Vincent said they should start on the business plan and outline every step carefully. Patrick agreed they should cover all bases and set it up for success.

Vincent does not have access to Patrick’s private thoughts, hidden motives, or any events he did not personally observe or hear about through Patrick or their interactions.
